findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repair review records an export problem as a P1 follow-up; a later review finds that the same problem exposes another customer's invoices and reports it as P0. The `key in followups` branch sets `follow_up` without checking the current severity. `score.holds` then treats the P0 as nonblocking, and `bound_review` skips it. If the earlier blocker is fixed, close can proceed despite the newly discovered data exposure.
findings.title: [P1] Do not restore follow-up status to an escalated P0

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A review reports `[P1] Saving a basket fails`, a repair review marks it fixed, and a later edit breaks the main save path, which the next reviewer reports as `[P0] Saving a basket fails` in the same file. This change makes the two titles share an identity. `src/forge/review.py:1043` then drops the P0 because that identity was previously marked fixed, before checking its severity or the intervening edit. The prior implementation kept these priority-tagged titles distinct, so this case newly allows close to miss the P0.
findings.title: [P1] Preserve a P0 when a fixed finding recurs with a priority tag
